comments.note: DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER_DEEP_AGENTS is defined in src/targets/types.ts (not frontmatter.ts as the WP stated) to follow the established pattern where all default frontmatter constants live in the targets layer. Placing it in frontmatter.ts would create a circular import: built-in.ts imports from targets/types.ts, so frontmatter.ts (builders layer) cannot be imported by targets/built-in.ts. The constant is re-exported from frontmatter.ts and builders/index.ts so the public API is unchanged.

Two existing tests (names() and allDefinitions()) were updated to reflect the now-3-entry default registry. Four new tests were added for the deep-agents target (has, outputDirKey, filenameContextKey, contextFlags). All 281 tests pass.

DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER_DEEP_AGENTS placed in src/targets/types.ts (not frontmatter.ts as originally scoped) to avoid circular import — design rationale is sound; re-exported from frontmatter.ts and builders/index.ts preserving public API.
Regression: 281 tests passed across 17 test files (0 failures).

comments.note: AC-4 coverage gap: tests/builders/target-variable-injection.test.ts tests target_vscode and target_claude_code injection via actual buildPersona calls but has no equivalent test for target_deep_agents. The test added in tests/targets/target-registry.test.ts verifies TargetDefinition.contextFlags (registry data), not the runtime injection path in buildContext (which uses `target_${target.replace(/-/g, '_')} = true`). The implementation is provably correct by inspection and the generic mechanism is tested for two other targets, but an explicit runtime test would close this gap.

Design observation: TargetDefinition.contextFlags is documented as key-value pairs automatically merged into the build context, but buildContext (persona-builder.ts:241) does NOT read from the registry's contextFlags at all — it injects a single boolean flag via string replacement regardless of what contextFlags contains. For the built-in targets this is consistent (contextFlags mirrors what the string replacement produces), but a custom target that sets contextFlags to { some_flag: 'value' } would NOT get that flag injected. This divergence should be resolved when the TargetRegistry is wired into the runtime.

summary: WP-007 passes review. Implementation correctly adds the deep-agents target as the third entry in the default registry, following the established pattern for built-in targets. All ACs verified.

Fix-Forward applied: TargetDefinition.contextFlags JSDoc in src/targets/types.ts corrected from 'automatically merged into the build context' to accurately state the field is declarative and not yet consumed by the runtime. tsc --noEmit remains clean.

Design quality is high: the placement of DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER_DEEP_AGENTS in targets/types.ts (rather than frontmatter.ts as originally specced) is architecturally sound and avoids a circular import. The re-export chain through frontmatter.ts and builders/index.ts preserves the public API surface. Test additions are thorough for the registry layer; one runtime injection test gap documented as documentation-forward.

comments.note: Fix-Forward: corrected TargetDefinition.contextFlags JSDoc in src/targets/types.ts. Previous text 'Key-value pairs automatically merged into the build context whenever this target is being rendered' is factually incorrect — the runtime (buildContext at persona-builder.ts:241) uses independent string replacement to inject exactly one boolean flag per target name; it does NOT read contextFlags from the registry. Replaced with accurate language: 'Declarative context flags — not yet consumed by the runtime.' This prevents consumers from relying on non-existent registry-driven injection.

[documentation-forward] tests/builders/target-variable-injection.test.ts tests target_vscode and target_claude_code runtime injection via actual buildPersona() calls but has no equivalent test for target_deep_agents. While correctness is guaranteed by the generic string replacement mechanism, an explicit test would close the coverage gap flagged by QA and serve as a regression guard if that injection path is refactored during the TargetRegistry wiring WP.

Architecture note for the wiring WP: when the runtime is updated to read contextFlags from the TargetRegistry, the precedence between the current string-replacement injection (target_name = true) and registry-provided contextFlags needs to be explicitly decided. Registry contextFlags should be the authoritative source; the string replacement pattern should be subsumed or removed to avoid two injection mechanisms for the same purpose.
